newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican debtor leader gets bail after jail stint.
newsitem.headline: Mexican debtor leader gets bail after jail stint.

text.p: The leader of a belligerent middle-class debtors group was released on bail on Tuesday after spending four days in jail when he tried to disrupt a meeting of powerful Mexican bankers.

Gerardo Fernandez Norona, head of the Citizens Assembly of Bank Debtors, was arrested on Friday on the first day of the Mexican Bankers Association annual convention in the Caribbean tourist resort of Cancun.
With a handful of supporters, he was planning to draw attention to the sky-high debts of many Mexicans in the wake of a 1994-1995 financial crisis.
State news agency Notimex said he was released on bail after facing charges of attacking three policemen, but there were political motives also involved in Fernandez Norona's arrest.

His colleagues at the bank convention told Reuters last week that they were followed by secret police and illegally arrested outside the convention center while President Ernesto Zedillo was addressing the bankers.

Notimex quoted Quintano Roo state Gov. Mario Villanueva as saying Fernandez Norona was held for "trying to boycott" the convention. "It's absolutely true that he was on the verge of damaging Cancun as a tourist destination," he said.
Notimex said Fernandez Norona planned to present a countersuit against state government officials for fabricating charges, illegal detention and kidnapping.

Last year, Fernandez Norona and his supporters broke into the convention, embarrassing bankers and top Finance Ministry officials as they protested the plight of millions of ordinary Mexicans affected by the crisis.
This year, a huge security cordon was thrown around the convention center to keep them out, and several hotels in Cancun refused to allow them lodging.
